diagnostics.message: :output.custom_role_id: explicit depends_on of :resource.google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles is redundant — already implied by attribute references

google_organization_iam_binding.authoritative bindings may reference custom roles defined via var.iam / var.group_iam (as "organizations/NNN/roles/<role_id>"), but it has no dependency on google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles. GCP fails the binding if the custom role does not exist yet, so the roles must be created first.

google_organization_iam_member.additive may grant custom roles created by this module (via var.iam_additive / var.iam_additive_members), but has no dependency on google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles. Applying the additive members before the custom roles exist would fail (or silently no-op) because the role is not yet defined in the organization.

google_organization_iam_policy.authoritative sets an authoritative policy whose bindings (from var.iam_bindings_authoritative) can reference custom roles created by this module, but it has no dependency on google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles. The authoritative policy would overwrite/fail against bindings for roles that do not yet exist.

output.custom_role_id's explicit depends_on on google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles is redundant: the output's value already iterates over that resource (google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles), so the dependency is already established via the attribute reference.
